_comment: TFT rule network, the part that holds in any set: the game's mechanics in general terms, the strategy principles that follow from them, and the checkpoint readings that show where a game stood, joined by typed edges. Each set adds data/sets/{set}/rule-network.season.json with the numbers (stage damage and the rest), its own mechanics, and wording that quotes them; src/coach/rule-network.ts merges the two. 'basis': riot = a Riot-published number; sums = arithmetic on Riot numbers; benchmark = a large-sample statistic; heuristic = expert rule of thumb; audit = measured in this player's games (data/core/rule-evidence.json). Principles are conditional: 'advice' is the usual answer, 'unless' when it is not.

edgeTypes.rests_on: The rule follows from this mechanic or principle.
edgeTypes.refines: A narrower, conditional version of the target.
edgeTypes.enables: Makes the target possible or cheaper.
edgeTypes.trades_off: The two pull against each other; neither is right on its own.
edgeTypes.overrides: When this rule's condition holds, the target's usual answer no longer applies.
edgeTypes.leads_to: A break or reading here makes the target reading more likely later in the same game. Used to trace a game.
edgeTypes.explains: The principle a symptom reading breaks.

nodes.name: Income
nodes.statement: Base income each round once the opening rounds are over, 1 gold for a won player round, and 1 gold of interest for every 10 gold held, up to a cap.

nodes.name: Streak gold
nodes.statement: Runs of wins or losses pay extra gold that rises with the length of the run, the same for wins and losses. A won round adds 1 on top.

nodes.name: Player damage
nodes.statement: A lost player round costs the stage's base damage plus 1 for each enemy unit left alive. Base damage rises from stage to stage.

nodes.name: Experience
nodes.statement: Gold buys XP at a fixed rate and every round gives some free. Each level costs more XP than the one before.

nodes.name: Shop odds and roll price
nodes.statement: A roll has a fixed price. Each level sets the odds of each unit cost, and each cost is most common at one level.

nodes.name: Shared pool
nodes.statement: Every player draws from one shared pool, with fewer copies of more expensive units. Three copies make a 2-star, nine a 3-star.

nodes.name: Board size
nodes.statement: You field as many units as your level.

nodes.name: Items
nodes.statement: Two components make one item and a unit holds three. A component in the item bench adds nothing to a fight.

nodes.name: Round structure
nodes.statement: From stage 2 each stage has seven rounds with a PvE round at x-7, and augments come on three fixed rounds. Stages 3 and 4 hold most of the game's player rounds.

nodes.name: Placement
nodes.statement: You place by how long you last. Players knocked out in the same round are ranked by the least negative HP, then by HP at the start of that round. Gold held when you are knocked out buys nothing.

nodes.name: HP is a budget that gets dearer
nodes.statement: A loss saves about the same gold in every stage but costs more HP as base damage rises. Spend HP early for gold; spend gold late to keep HP.
nodes.advice: Bleed in stage 2 if it buys something; from stage 3 on, treat each loss as expensive.
nodes.unless: Your gold cannot change the fight, in which case the HP is gone either way.

nodes.name: Count the losses you have left
nodes.statement: Losses left is your HP divided by what a loss costs at this stage, rounded up, minus one. It is the clock every spend decision runs on.
nodes.advice: Recount at 3-1 and 4-1, and whenever a stage's price is about to rise.

nodes.name: Stabilize above the next stage's floor
nodes.statement: Keep enough HP for two losses at the next stage's prices.
nodes.advice: Once HP falls under the next stage's floor, stop paying HP for gold and spend.
nodes.unless: Players below you are about to go out, which buys room your HP number does not show.

nodes.name: Spend when it changes the fight
nodes.statement: Gold and board strength feed each other. Spending is right when it flips the next fight, and holding is right when you would win or lose anyway.
nodes.advice: Before spending, ask whether it changes the next fight, not whether you can afford it.

nodes.name: Bank to the next ten
nodes.statement: Each 10 gold held pays 1 a round, so end rounds on 10, 20, 30, 40 or 50 while HP is cheap. The roll that crosses a ten also costs a round of interest.
nodes.advice: Stop rolls and purchases on a ten in stages 2 and 3.
nodes.unless: HP is under the next stage's floor or the fight decides whether you survive.

nodes.name: Don't roll in stage 2 without a reason
nodes.statement: Gold is worth most early, so rolling before stage 3 needs a reason: pairs to finish or a streak to protect.
nodes.advice: Keep early gold for levels and the stage 3 spike.

nodes.name: Gold above the interest cap earns nothing
nodes.statement: Interest stops at its cap, so gold held above it while losing buys no income and costs HP.
nodes.advice: Above the cap while losing, put the excess into levels or rolls.
nodes.unless: You are saving for a named roll-down round in the next round or two.

nodes.name: A bank can't help once you are out
nodes.statement: Gold held when you are knocked out buys nothing. On your last losses, interest has only a round or two left to pay.
nodes.advice: With one or two losses left, spend what the next fight needs; below about 20 HP that is usually everything.
nodes.unless: Nothing you can buy changes the fight.

nodes.name: Commit to a streak or don't count on one
nodes.statement: Streak gold rises with the length of the run, so the pay sits at the end of it, and trading wins and losses pays none.
nodes.advice: In stage 2, play to win every fight or plan the losses; don't drift between them.

nodes.name: A broken win streak costs more than one round
nodes.statement: Losing one round on a long win streak costs that round's gold, the streak gold of the next rounds, and the HP.
nodes.advice: On a long win streak, spend to keep it when the spend holds several fights.
nodes.unless: The spend only delays the loss by one round.

nodes.name: A loss streak needs a stage 2 start and a named flip round
nodes.statement: The same losses cost more HP each stage for the same streak gold. Without a planned flip, a loss streak becomes the poverty loop: low HP and a weak board.
nodes.advice: Lose on purpose only in stage 2, and name the round you flip before the streak starts.
nodes.unless: A trait or augment pays for losses.

nodes.name: Flip a loss streak with a board that holds
nodes.statement: Alternating wins and losses after a long loss streak pays little streak gold and still costs fights.
nodes.advice: Flip when the gold buys a board that wins several in a row.

nodes.name: Pick one spike in stages 3 and 4 and land it
nodes.statement: Stages 3 and 4 pay less gold than the levels and upgrades you want cost, so only one plan fits, and a board that keeps losing has to spend early in the stretch.
nodes.advice: At 3-1 count your losses left, name your spike round, and spend before stage 5, not in it.
nodes.unless: Your board is winning fights, which pays for a later spike.

nodes.name: Roll at your carry's level
nodes.statement: Roll at the level where your carry's cost is most common in the shop.
nodes.advice: Level first when the better odds still leave enough gold to roll.

nodes.name: Level timings are a plan, not a schedule
nodes.statement: Standard level timings shift with streaks and comp, and players who finish top 4 and bottom 4 differ little in level at any stage.
nodes.advice: Choose the curve your comp and HP call for; don't chase a round number.

nodes.name: A level needs gold behind it
nodes.statement: Better odds only repay a level if gold is left to roll on them; every level is rolls you did not make.
nodes.advice: Don't buy the level that leaves too little to roll for the units it unlocks.

nodes.name: Roll when HP can't pay for another miss
nodes.statement: With two losses or fewer left and a fight that looks lost, a bank is worth less than the fight.
nodes.advice: Roll what the next fight needs.
nodes.unless: Nothing in the pool can flip the fight.

nodes.name: Roll when you hold pairs
nodes.statement: A held pair cuts the gold a 2-star costs by more than half. With four or more pairs a short roll is cheap insurance.
nodes.advice: Plan the spike around the pairs you hold.

nodes.name: Pick where you stop before you roll
nodes.statement: Each set of rolls finds less than the last, and rebuilding from 0 to 30 gold takes about six rounds against two from 20.
nodes.advice: Stop when the fight is won, on a ten, or above the price of what you hunt; roll to 0 only on your last losses.

nodes.name: Slow roll only once the board holds
nodes.statement: A 3-star of a cheap unit costs more than one bank, so it is rolled from income above a ten over several rounds.
nodes.advice: Start slow rolling when the board is winning or holding HP, not before.

nodes.name: Play your strongest board
nodes.statement: Field the strongest board the stage allows without giving up the next spike. Each enemy unit you kill is 1 HP saved even in a loss.
nodes.advice: Field the best units you hold every round; a narrower loss is cheaper.

nodes.name: Fill every slot
nodes.statement: Board size equals level, so an empty slot is XP paid for nothing.
nodes.advice: Field a unit in every slot, even a cheap one.

nodes.name: Judge your board against the boards you fight
nodes.statement: Strength is relative: a board worth less than the boards it meets loses whatever its absolute value.
nodes.advice: When your board is clearly weaker than the boards you fight, the next spend should go into the board.

nodes.name: Upgrades before trait breakpoints
nodes.statement: A 2-star with weaker traits usually beats a 1-star with the perfect trait.
nodes.advice: Don't hold a weak unit only to reach a breakpoint when a 2-star can take its slot.

nodes.name: Keep only units you will play
nodes.statement: Bench units are gold that is not fighting or earning interest.
nodes.advice: Sell what you will not field; keep pairs of your line.

nodes.name: Slam items for tempo
nodes.statement: A finished item fights; a component does not. Waiting for the perfect item costs HP now.
nodes.advice: Build an item whenever you hold more than four components, picking items many units can use.

nodes.name: Concentrate items on the units that use them
nodes.statement: Damage items belong on the carry that deals the damage, durability items on the tanks.
nodes.advice: Give the carry its items by stage 4 and don't spread damage items thin.

nodes.name: Pick augments for the game you are in
nodes.statement: Economy and item augments pay most on the first augment round; later, an augment that stabilizes a losing board beats more gold.
nodes.advice: Check HP and recent losses before comparing the three offers.

nodes.name: Contested lines cost more to hit
nodes.statement: Each player on your units draws from the same pool, and the fewer copies a unit has, the more each extra player raises the cost of a 2-star.
nodes.advice: With two or more others on your carry, look for a line that uses your items.

nodes.name: Pivot toward what you hold, a stage early
nodes.statement: A finished 2-star on another line beats a 1-star on a contested one. Pivots are cheapest in stage 3, planned from scouting, with flexible items.
nodes.advice: Move toward pairs you hold; don't switch plans every round.

nodes.name: Tanks die first, the carry dies last
nodes.statement: Durable units in front, the carry behind them where it hits what matters.
nodes.advice: Field a frontline every round from stage 4.

nodes.name: Position against the board you meet
nodes.statement: Scout the next opponent's carry, backline access and area damage, and place your units against them.
nodes.advice: When the same opponent beats you twice, move the carry or the tanks.

nodes.name: Outlast the players below you
nodes.statement: Placement is relative: your HP only has to outlast the players below you.
nodes.advice: Judge HP and level against the living players, and count who can go out before you.

nodes.name: Heavy stage 2 bleed
nodes.statement: More than about 15 HP lost during stage 2.

nodes.name: Low HP entering stage 4
nodes.statement: Under 60 HP at 4-1.

nodes.name: Under 25 HP entering stage 5
nodes.statement: Two losses or fewer from going out as stage 5 raises the price of a loss.

nodes.name: Under the next stage's floor
nodes.statement: HP fell below two losses at the next stage's prices.

nodes.name: Knocked out holding gold
nodes.statement: Gold was still in the bank when the game ended.
